steps.text: The empty silence leaves one feeling colder than ever. The reporter's heavy bag slows her down, her footsteps upon the snow clear for all to hear.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Less people than before, even here...

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: ...Hmm?

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Miss! Sorry to bother you, can I ask you a few quick questions?

steps.name: Rushed Local
steps.text: About?

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Right now, Karlan Trade—

steps.name: Rushed Local
steps.text: I'd rather not have to hear that name.

steps.name: Rushed Local
steps.text: Sir Enciodes needs to come out and go over why he signed those agreements already.

steps.name: Rushed Local
steps.text: 'Resources for development', what rubbish. All we got for our resources was a Catastrophe. How's he going to explain that, huh?
By the time the reporter finishes digesting the lady's angry words, she has already long-since left with a swish of her cloak.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: ...Excuse me, sir!

steps.name: Kind Local
steps.text: Ah, you're one of those reporters from Victoria?

steps.name: Kind Local
steps.text: Kjerag's not been the kindest place, lately. Even us locals prefer holing up at home. You best take care.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: It's times like these where I can't be afraid, otherwise I'm not fit to hold this camera.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: ...But thanks for the heads-up, anyhow. What I'd like to know is, how do you see Enciodes right now, in your honest opinion?

steps.name: Kind Local
steps.text: Hmm... Sorry, Miss, I think he's cheated Kjerag, but Victoria's worth doubting too.

steps.name: Kind Local
steps.text: I've seen how big the changes here have been these past few years. If you said Enciodes hasn't had any difficulty making those changes, then I'd say you're wrong.

steps.name: Kind Local
steps.text: If only the Great Elder of the Court could come out and say a few words, it'd all be fine—
A stone flies right past the tip of the reporter's nose all of a sudden, smashing the store window behind her.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Eek—!

steps.name: Angry Local
steps.text: Get out of Kjerag, Victorian scum!

steps.name: Angry Local
steps.text: Enciodes, the Vine-Bead Court, us, we've all got nothing to do with you!

steps.name: Angry Local
steps.text: Still got the stones to take pictures?! Get the faen off our land already!

spans.text: Still got the stones to take pictures?! Get the

steps.text: Nothing has left her with complicated feelings more than this moment.
She has seen the ordinary people of Kjerag slowly become more mistrustful, more on-edge.
Yet she has also seen once-trusted members of the camera crew sneak into her room to inspect her drafts and camera, over and over.
As the man picks up yet another stone, she bows goodbye to her interviewee, and runs away from the scene...
It seems her only choice is to escape... but escape to where?

steps.name: Local Child
steps.text: Are you Victorian, miss?

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Ah... Hello there.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Do... you hate Victoria?

steps.name: Local Child
steps.text: Nope, I don't.
A dirty little hand reaches out to her, with a piece of stale Victorian bread sitting in the palm.

steps.name: Local Child
steps.text: But my pappa told me to throw these all away. He said we wouldn't have any Victorian charity in our house.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Then...

steps.name: Local Child
steps.text: But Kjeragandr taught us to love our neighbors, and repay kindness with kindness.

steps.name: Local Child
steps.text: So, I wanted to give it back to you.
As she watches the child hurry away, the reporter feels as if the dry bread in her hand is choking her throat. Her eyelids tremble, and she clenches her teeth...

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: Get her in the car. Don't let anyone see.
That is the last thing she remembers hearing before she loses consciousness.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Sorry for bothering you with yet another visit, Mr. Silverash.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Perhaps you would rather be seeing some other pretty face during all this hubbub...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: There is no need to be so humble.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Kjerag is indebted to you for your care, and I had hoped for the chance to express my gratitude.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hardly, hardly... It seems my long-awaited return has left me awash with churning emotion once more.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I would like nothing more than to be the bearer of good news every time I come over, before throwing my old bones into the mountains for some peace and quiet.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But life is a fickle thing, and it demands we improvise, does it not?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I do believe you are here to give me some bad news, Lord Viscount, but not in the name of Caster.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hmph, I'd rather not get mixed up with that old lady's affairs again.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Though based on what went on the last time I was here... It's her who doesn't want to get mixed up with me.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: With all that said, My Lord...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, yes, on to business, I know you're a busy man.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I am here to bid you farewell, Mr. Silverash.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If the recent shift in public opinion against Victoria has troubled you, then I can—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: No, no, no, nothing of the sort...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...I had hoped against hope that old Caster was also reaching the age where she spoke from the heart.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: That tends to bring a bit of sweetness to the tongue, no? But as you can see, things have come to this.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Though I may seem a dotard these days, I still find myself compelled to ask you one thing...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Is there truly no other way?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You know her plans involve more than just a few mines, My Lord.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: From the moment she laid hands on Ensia, this negotiation has become wholly unacceptable to me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: So how do you plan to handle her? Are you really prepared to cross swords with her?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You know better than I that if we do not keep the idea of 'crossing swords' on the table, then Kjerag may as well already be in her pocket.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Of course I do...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh* What to say, what to say...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Knowing how the old lady is, she will never let your little tiff go now that it's reached this stage.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I truly am worried for you, Sir Enciodes. Whatever shall you do next?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What is there to do but to seize the opportunity?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Since you have mentioned her, you are also an old acquaintance of Her Grace, are you not?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hardly know her.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A few years back, we'd chat about family matters, and she'd always grumble to me about how none of the young Casters were worth a damn.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The less useful they turn out to be, the more hasty she gets in doing things. Who would have guessed that she was known as a complete enigma in her youth...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I had a brief encounter with Her Grace a decade or so ago. Her grandeur strikes me even now.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hah, no need to butter her up to me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I am fully aware that her high-and-mighty noble posturing is something she can never change.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: No matter how many schemes are brewing behind the scenes, one must always keep one's face haughty and dignified.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Well, that's that. I'm sure your people have more urgent things to trouble you with. I should be heading off right about now.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This talk of ours has been productive, My Lord.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I hope I will have a more suitable opportunity in the future to invite you to Kjerag.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, couldn't ask for better!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, yes...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: (Quietly) When you next see Her Grace, by no means tell her I've been calling her 'old' behind her back.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: ...I would never, Lord Viscount.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Atta boy.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I too, am really looking forward to the chance to visit Kjerag again.

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: Yes, nobody saw us.

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: It was no trouble, Matriarch. Your request is my—

steps.name: Indistinct Voice
steps.text: I'll bring her over right away.
Hey, wakey-wakey!

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: ...I...This is... I was at—

steps.name: Browntail Guard
steps.text: Half a day's sleep not enough for you? Get up, our Matriarch has things she wants to ask you.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Who... brought me here...?
Hmph. How long will it take you to learn a gentle touch?

steps.name: Browntail Guard
steps.text: I-I'm sorry.

steps.name: Browntail Guard
steps.text: Matriarch.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Hey, you awake yet?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: No thrashing about, unless you feel like the ropes around your wrists aren't chafing enough.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Ah, Ratatos!

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: ...Matriarch Ratatos. I thought you were—

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Not a single burn on me. Real surprising, isn't it?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: When you get the chance, tell your colleagues that when dealing with the Browntails, best check the room for tricks.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: My... colleagues?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Be honest now, my little spy. What were you hoping to capture on that camera of yours, all those days you were sneaking about?

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Wait, what... No, you misunderstand me, Madam! How could I be a spy?!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: That's what all the other spies we got said too.
The guards rifle through the reporter's back and throw its contents onto the floor: the photos she has taken and developed the past few days.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: We wouldn't care much about you if you take pictures of local traditions or even patrolling guards.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: But you didn't hesitate before taking a bunch of pictures of the Vine-Bead Court. You even went to a few mountains, clicking that shutter of yours.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Don't think I don't know anything.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Matriarch Ratatos, whether you believe me or not, I really am nothing more than a regular reporter.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: If I was a spy, why would I be walking around with all this evidence on me?

spans.text: a spy, why would I be walking around with all this evidence on me?

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: With all this chaos going on right now, I could have easily given it all to my colleagues at the TV station.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: That's what you need to explain.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Fact of the matter is, you were carrying a great deal of suspicious material, and had a very strange itinerary. How do I know you weren't trying to flee?

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Because I'm trying to protect that material!

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: The Duke of Caster wants control over public opinion. The news office sent people to join the camera crew, and they've been sneaking into my room to edit my pictures.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: If I didn't try to get away, most of them would be confiscated, maybe even used to misrepresent things here.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Everything they do is to whitewash Victoria trying to strong-arm its way into Kjerag!

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: If you think these pictures will be of any use to Kjerag, you can have them all.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: I just want you to release them, to let more people know what's going on here...

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: It doesn't need Victoria's 'support', but real, actual help!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: That might be tricky.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Is Enciodes able to take a call right now?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: He has more pressing matters to handle, so he sent me as support.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: After my lovely funeral, I handed the spies we captured over to him. According to our agreement, he was supposed to send backup.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: And in the end, he only sent one woman, even if she is the Black Knight.

spans.text: And in the end, he only sent one woman, even if she

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Not sure if I should call him generous or stingy here...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: So, what's his plan for dealing with Caster?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: We're still gathering information on our enemy. I was also sent here to help with your interrogations.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The most critical thing to find out now, is if this reporter has taken any photos of 'things in the mountains'.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Ah, yes, our little friend here...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I can untie your restraints, but first, you need to promise me...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: You'll answer all my questions. That sound alright to you?
